chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.
And that the masjids are Allah's, therefore do not call upon anyone along with Allah.
He عليه السلام said: "They are the successors."

key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءُ: the successors, i.e. the divinely designated successors
key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدَ: the masjids; interpreted here in a deeper referential sense
key_terms.فَلَا تَدْعُوا: so do not invoke or call upon

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام interpret the verse "And that the masjids are Allah's"?
ai.summary: This hadith presents an interpretation of the verse by identifying "the masjids" with the awsiya' (successors). It highlights a Wilayah-centered reading in which the verse points to divinely appointed authorities and their sacred status in relation to devotion to Allah.
